entities.name: Emhyr var Emreis
aliases: White Flame Dancing on the Graves of His Enemies

facts.text: Ciri escaped the Aen Elle world by using her growing ability to travel between worlds.
Eredin gathered the Wild Hunt to chase Ciri after she fled, but failed to catch her.
After escaping Eredin, Ciri became lost, wandering through unknown times and places.
Ciri entered a portal in the Tower of the Swallow hoping to reach Thanedd, but instead arrived in the world of the Aen Elle.
The Aen Elle are also known as the Alder Folk.
In the Aen Elle world, Ciri became a pawn in a political conflict between the sage Avallac'h and Eredin Breacc Glas, leader of the Wild Hunt.
The Aen Elle claimed a debt on Ciri's blood, believing her ancestor Lara Dorren owed them for betraying Ithlinne's prophecy.
To return home from the Aen Elle world, Ciri would have needed to give their leader a child with power over the Gate of the Worlds.
Avallac'h claimed his goal in using the Gate of the Worlds was to save the Aen Seidhe elves and humans from the White Frost.
Eredin's true motives for controlling the Gate of the Worlds were suspected to be conquest of other worlds rather than salvation.
The Aen Elle had once before mastered the Gate of the Worlds and used it to conquer another world.
After wandering lost, Ciri ended up at the gates of Stygga Citadel, where Vilgefortz was hiding.
When Ciri confronted Vilgefortz at Stygga Citadel, Geralt and his companions arrived to aid her, and Yennefer escaped captivity to join them.
Yennefer had not participated in the coup at Thanedd, contrary to rumor; she had instead been searching for Ciri and was captured by treacherous former allies.
The Battle of Stygga Citadel ended with Vilgefortz's defeat and death at Geralt's hands.
Milva, Cahir, Regis, and Angouleme died during the Battle of Stygga Citadel.
After the Battle of Stygga Citadel, Emperor Emhyr var Emreis arrived with imperial soldiers, having learned of Vilgefortz's treachery and his collusion with Stefan Skellen.
Emperor Emhyr var Emreis unexpectedly showed mercy and let Geralt, Yennefer, and Ciri leave unharmed after looking at his daughter Ciri's face.
The Rivia Pogrom occurred on 25 September 1268.
The Rivia Pogrom was sparked when a dwarven stallholder insulted noblewoman and war orphan Nadia Esposita.
The initial brawl from the insult to Nadia Esposita escalated into a riot that spread into the Elm district of Rivia.
Professor Emmerich Gottshalk recorded that 184 people died in the hour before Triss Merigold intervened in the Rivia Pogrom, half of them women and children.
Boethius of Lyria argued the Rivia Pogrom was a planned provocation, with weapons smuggled in and distributed to human rioters directed at nonhuman districts.
Master Casper Dubhen argued the Rivia Pogrom resulted from common human traits like ignorance and xenophobia rather than conspiracy.
The Rivia Pogrom killed almost two hundred people, mostly nonhumans.
During the Rivia Pogrom, Geralt was mortally wounded by a man he had just spared, who stabbed him with a pitchfork while Geralt tried to stop the mob.
Yennefer tried to save the dying Geralt with magic during the Rivia Pogrom, nearly killing herself from exhaustion.
Ciri saved Geralt and Yennefer by transporting them outside of time and space during the Rivia Pogrom, then vanished from the world herself.
Several years after the Rivia Pogrom, Geralt reappeared near Kaer Morhen, alive but with partial amnesia.
After the Rivia Pogrom, the Wild Hunt led by Eredin continued searching for Ciri.
Geralt and Yennefer took refuge on the Isle of Avalon, which Ciri had prepared for them.
The Wild Hunt kidnapped Yennefer to try to lure Ciri out of hiding.
Geralt pursued the Wild Hunt across many worlds while searching for Yennefer.
Geralt saved the life of witcher Letho of Gulet during a battle with a monster, earning help from three witchers of the School of the Viper.
Geralt offered himself in exchange for Yennefer's freedom, and Eredin took him prisoner instead.
Ciri devised a plan to rescue Geralt from the Wild Hunt, allowing him to escape back to his world, though he lost his memory in the process.
Geralt found shelter at Kaer Morhen with his Wolf School companions, but Triss Merigold's magic could not restore his lost memory.
Azar Javed, a renegade mage, and an assassin known as the Professor led a surprise attack on Kaer Morhen.
The attackers on Kaer Morhen stole secrets of witcher mutations from the keep's laboratory.
A witcher died defending Kaer Morhen during the attack by Azar Javed and the Professor.
Geralt traveled to Vizima, capital of Temeria, seeking King Foltest, who was absent from the city.
During Foltest's absence, Jacques de Aldersberg, grandmaster of the Order of the Flaming Rose, increased persecution of nonhumans in Vizima.
Increased persecution of nonhumans in Vizima drove elves and dwarves to join local Scoia'tael bands.
Fisstech is a white powder drug widely used across the Continent, described by City Guard captain Vincent Meiss of Vizima.
Geralt discovered that the Salamandra, a criminal syndicate dealing in fisstech, extortion, and contract killings, was behind the Kaer Morhen attack.
Geralt destroyed the Salamandra's fisstech labs and killed its members, working up to the leadership.
Geralt killed the Professor in revenge for the witcher slain at Kaer Morhen.
Geralt confronted and eventually killed Azar Javed, who revealed Jacques de Aldersberg as the mastermind behind the plot.
Jacques de Aldersberg was breeding mutants using stolen witcher secrets to suppress the nonhuman riots he had incited.
Jacques de Aldersberg was revealed to be a source, a person born with innate magical power.
Jacques de Aldersberg trapped Geralt in a magical illusion depicting the frozen world after the apocalyptic White Frost.
Jacques de Aldersberg's ultimate goal was to breed a new race of supermen able to survive the White Frost prophesied by Ithlinne.
Geralt refused Jacques de Aldersberg's offer to join him and killed him with a witcher's blade.
After Jacques de Aldersberg's death, an assassin who turned out to be a mutated witcher attempted to kill King Foltest, but Geralt stopped the attack.
King Foltest made Geralt his personal bodyguard after the failed assassination attempt against him.
King Demavend of Aedirn was assassinated, and about a month later King Foltest was also killed.
Geralt was falsely accused of murdering King Foltest and imprisoned, but escaped to find the real assassin.
Geralt traveled to the border town of Flotsam and discovered the assassin was Letho of Gulet, a witcher and former companion he no longer remembered.
Letho of Gulet fled Flotsam by forcing Triss Merigold to teleport them both to the Kingdom of Aedirn.
In Aedirn, Geralt encountered Saskia, the Virgin of Aedirn, leading an uprising amid conflict with King Henselt of Kaedwen.
King Henselt of Kaedwen seized Aedirnian territory after King Demavend's death.
Geralt discovered that two more Viper School witchers, confederates of Letho, were active in the Aedirn conflict.
Geralt fought and the three Viper School witchers settled their differences with blades.
Before dying, the Viper witchers revealed that Sile de Tansarville of the Lodge of Sorceresses had hired them to kill King Demavend.
The trails of Sile de Tansarville and Letho of Gulet led to the ancient ruins of Loc Muinne, site of a summit of Northern kings and sorceresses.
The Loc Muinne summit included delegates from Kaedwen, Aedirn, Temeria, and Redania, along with Nilfgaardian observers.
The Loc Muinne summit aimed to resolve the Temerian succession and consider reactivating the Conclave and Supreme Council of Sorcerers.
The Loc Muinne summit collapsed after Nilfgaardian intervention and was ended by a dragon attack.
Emperor Emhyr var Emreis orchestrated the assassination plot against the Northern kings using Viper School witchers, promising to help rebuild their keep.
The Lodge of Sorceresses' involvement in Demavend's assassination was separate private scheming that Emperor Emhyr exploited.
Emperor Emhyr's plot weakened both the Northern monarchs and the mages, clearing the way for his renewed invasion of the North.
During his conversation with Letho, Geralt learned that Yennefer was likely alive in the Nilfgaardian Empire.
Taking advantage of the Temerian interregnum and Northern discord, the Nilfgaardian army crossed the Yaruga river to invade the North again.
Yennefer sent Geralt a letter requesting a meeting in the former Temerian town of Willoughby.
While traveling through occupied Temeria, Geralt reunited with his mentor Vesemir.
Willoughby had been destroyed in fighting between Northern armies and Nilfgaard, and Yennefer was not there when Geralt and Vesemir arrived.
Geralt found Yennefer in the village of White Orchard after dealing with a griffin menacing locals and Nilfgaardian troops.
Yennefer was accompanied by Nilfgaardian guards who told Geralt that Emperor Emhyr needed to see them both.
Geralt and Yennefer were ambushed by the Wild Hunt while traveling to meet Emperor Emhyr in Vizima.
Emperor Emhyr revealed that Ciri had returned to their world and asked Geralt to find her.
Emhyr and Yennefer had already been searching for Ciri but stopped after their efforts attracted the Wild Hunt.
Emperor Emhyr offered Geralt gold to find Ciri, though Geralt needed no incentive to help her.
Ciri's presence was tracked through the war-torn region of Velen, the Free City of Novigrad, and the Skellige Islands.
Ciri first arrived back in this world in Skellige, causing a magical explosion that devastated part of the islands.
Ciri fled to Velen, where she encountered the Crones, three demonic sisters.
After escaping the Crones, Ciri found shelter with the Bloody Baron in Velen.
The Bloody Baron recommended Ciri seek help in Novigrad.
In Novigrad, Ciri sought help from Dandelion to lift a curse.
Dandelion was captured by guards of the Church of the Eternal Fire and imprisoned after covering Ciri's escape.
Geralt and Zoltan Chivay devised a plan to rescue Dandelion from imprisonment.
Avallac'h became Ciri's crucial ally in her flight from the Wild Hunt, putting him in open conflict with Eredin.
Avallac'h is an Aen Saevherne, a powerful elven mage-sage.
During a clash with the Wild Hunt, Avallac'h was cursed, deforming his body and mind.
Geralt, with Yennefer's help, lifted the curse afflicting Avallac'h.
After being cured, Avallac'h revealed that he had hidden Ciri on the Isle of Mists, outside time and space, to protect her.
Ciri lay in a magically induced sleep on the Isle of Mists until Geralt arrived and his presence broke the spell, waking her.
After reuniting, Geralt and Ciri returned to Kaer Morhen, but Eredin tracked them there with the Wild Hunt.
Imlerith, one of Eredin's commanders, led the Wild Hunt's assault on Kaer Morhen and killed Vesemir.
Grieving Vesemir's death, Ciri unleashed her dormant Power, devastating the attacking Wild Hunt forces and forcing them to retreat.
Geralt and his allies later hunted down and killed Imlerith to weaken the Wild Hunt.
Avallac'h convinced the Wild Hunt general Ge'els to stay out of the final conflict.
Geralt and his allies recruited the surviving Lodge of Sorceresses to help summon and trap the Naglfar, Eredin's vessel for traveling between worlds.
The final battle against the Wild Hunt took place off the shores of Skellige.
Geralt used a magic elven artifact to summon the Naglfar into a trap in a Skellige bay.
The Lodge of Sorceresses' magic prevented the Naglfar from fleeing while the imperial fleet blocked its escape to open sea.
Geralt boarded the Naglfar and dueled Eredin, ultimately killing him and breaking the power of the Wild Hunt for good.
Skellige mythology describes an apocalyptic prophecy called Tedd Deireadh, involving the Naglfar ship, the hero Hemdall, and a final conflict called Ragh Nar Roog.
